task_s.response:
1、Over the 30-day period, days with exercise had a higher average sleep score (77.5) compared to days without exercise (70.8), indicating an association between exercise and better sleep quality.
2、Exercise days showed substantially fewer sleep apnea events: only 50% of exercise days had any apnea events (average 0.67 events per night), versus 91.7% of sedentary days (average 1.42 events per night), suggesting a link between exercise and reduced apnea frequency.
3、Among exercise types, running days consistently had no apnea events and high sleep scores (average 79.8), while swimming days tended to have lower sleep scores (average 71.7) and continued apnea events; however, small sample sizes for individual types limit type-specific conclusions.
4、Overall, the data support a positive association between engaging in structured exercise and both higher sleep scores and fewer sleep apnea events, though causation cannot be inferred from this observational dataset.
